key_insight: Conditioning neural fields on latent states enables mesh-agnostic PDE dynamics models with grid-independent Lipschitz bounds, while exposing an expressivity–stability trade-off.
engineering_relevance: These models offer compact reduced-order PDE surrogates that can be evaluated across spatial discretizations without tying inference to a fixed mesh.
method: Represent spatial solutions with neural fields conditioned on evolving latent states.
Unify weak, strong, and pure conditioning within a meshless latent dynamics framework.
Prove universal approximation and derive conditioning-dependent Lipschitz stability bounds.
evidence_signal: Tests on Burgers’ equation, cylinder-flow Navier–Stokes, and linear advection report comparable or better accuracy than mesh-based models using only 2% of their trainable parameters, with nearly constant error across spatial discretizations.
watch_item: More expressive conditioning can weaken stability and potentially degrade temporal extrapolation; grid-independent bounds do not guarantee long-horizon accuracy.
paper_title: Meshless Latent Dynamics Models for Model Order Reduction of time-dependent Partial Differential Equations
